title: Subterranean Living Quarters (Dream Experience)
content: I dreamed over a year ago now of subterranean dormitories, and the impression it gave has stuck with me so strongly ever since. The earliest I can recall in the dream, I was outside in a terrain that looks like what I’ve seen in photos of rural northeast North Korea. It was desolate and dry and deathly quiet, and oddly cold. I remember I was nervous, I had been instructed to wait for someone to come lead me to where I would be living. I was holding a small bundle of items wrapped in a wool blanket, I believe it was the belongings I was allowed to take with me. I was eventually met by a very pleasant middle-aged man with graying hair who led me into this small flat building and down some stairs. There was a landing with elevators and we took them down to the deepest level they would go, then exited and crossed into another bank of elevators that went deeper. This continued several times. Each level seemed to have hallways that extended off either side from the elevator banks and turned corners. It felt sparsely decorated, I think maybe one floor-set vase with fake gladioli in it and a little end table with a lamp. The further down we went, the decor became a little more elaborate, with some forgettable still life paintings in ornate frames sometimes above the end table. Occasionally we would see other people waiting for elevators or rounding the corners past the vases and artwork, but they would either be in pairs conversing quietly or alone and silent with their heads down. Nobody paid any attention to us, and as far as I recall, even the few times people entered the elevators with us they didn’t speak to us or us to them. Eventually we entered yet another elevator and the man I was with pressed the button for not the lowest level available, but close to it. We exited the elevators and took a left around the corner past a large framed painting and vase of silk flowers. The hallway had vaulted ceilings and these huge floor-to-ceiling ornate carved doors. They almost looked like cabinets painted bright colors and carved with floral patterns like Black Forest cuckoo clocks. The man led me to one of these doors painted yellow and green and pulled it open by hooking his hand under the carvings. Inside was a very long room with a window at the end looking out to the terrain where I had been standing at the start of the dream (which makes no sense given how far underground we were at this point). I have to assume the window was simulated, and even in the dream it felt…fake somehow. Lining the walls on either side of the narrow walkway in the center were what looked to be extremely wide lockers that stretched from the floor almost to the vaulted ceiling. The lockers were at least two average-sized people wide and made of gray felt like cubicle dividers with white number plates on them. The man led me to a locker and pressed it to pop the door open. Inside was a small bed and a desk and a chair with a plain lamp. It was my living quarters. He then pressed the locker on the opposite side of the center walkway to show me it was his family’s living quarters where his wife and two small children were sitting on their bed reading books together. The whole dream had this pervasive feeling of being resigned to imprisonment. It was like everybody living there was trapped by an outside entity and forced to act like it was a great living situation. The man had been so pleasant and kind, but he looked exhausted and his smile seemed forced, like he was told to be cheery *or else*. And I remember having this trapped desperation welling up in my throat when I saw where I would be living, but also knowing that this would be my life now and I would have to make the best of things. The dream ended with me closing the door to my living space and crawling into the bed to cry myself to sleep.
